page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.12xlarge is an ARM-based, memory-optimized instance powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro system, this server configuration features 768 GB of memory, delivering a high 16:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 16 GB allocated per core. It integrates 2,850 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and maintains a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps, operating without hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core computational scaling, highlighted by a top-quartile multi-core stress-ng score of 72,810.23 alongside 54.59 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded throughput shows lower baseline performance, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 955.0 and bottom-quartile results in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression tests. Memory throughput benchmarks show middle-tier performance, reaching 144.33 GB/sec in uncached read operations and 71.96 GB/sec in uncached writes.

The physical-core design eliminates hyperthreading contention, yielding predictable execution for multi-threaded systems while optimizing memory density. However, software stacks dependent on x86 instruction extensions such as AVX-512 will experience architectural limitations. The platform is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise databases, in-memory key-value caches like Redis, real-time analytics engines, and workloads requiring high-capacity NVMe scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on 48 dedicated ARM64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 768 GB of system memory, establishing a 16:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 2,850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps of baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core compute throughput and high-throughput Redis operations, balanced against lower single-threaded processing metrics. Because it provides 16 GB of memory per dedicated physical core without hardware multithreading, it delivers consistent resource allocation for high-footprint workloads. The server is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, distributed data processing, and enterprise workloads that demand extensive RAM capacity coupled with fast local NVMe storage.
